trials.notes: Used the recommended WP_HTML_Tag_Processor template pattern: existing src/alt placeholders preserve attribute order, a text placeholder gives set_modifiable_text() a #text token to replace, and get_updated_html() retrieves queued edits. All called methods are documented. Minor deduction only for unnecessary defensive fallback and not checking set_modifiable_text()'s return, though the #text guard makes it effectively safe here.

Closest to the canonical documented pattern. Correct processor, documented methods only, plain values passed to set_attribute() and set_modifiable_text(), and get_updated_html() used rather than serialization. Handles documented encoding and placeholder-text concerns cleanly.

All methods used are documented across the two rendered files, including create_fragment(), token walking, inherited mutation APIs, and get_updated_html(). The main deduction is processor choice: the docs recommend the lighter Tag Processor for flat template/attribute work, while HTML Processor is intended for structural parsing. The implementation is still idiomatic enough to pass because the template is fixed and supported.

failure_analysis:
No hidden case failed in any trial: all three passed simple, ampersand-in-caption, quotes-in-alt, special-chars-in-url, angle-brackets-in-caption, unicode, and html-in-caption-not-parsed.

The docs did well on the exact failure-prone points for this task. The Tag Processor's “Building markup from a template” section directly explains filling untrusted values into a known shape through the API, preserving attribute order by including empty attributes in the template, and including placeholder text so set_modifiable_text() has a #text token to replace. The set_attribute() docs clearly state that callers should pass normal unescaped strings and that new attributes sort by name, which prevents the common src/alt order bug. The set_modifiable_text() docs clearly state that ordinary containers like FIGCAPTION do not carry text themselves and that text must be written on a #text token, preventing the common mistake of calling it while positioned on the FIGCAPTION tag. The get_updated_html() docs also steer models away from serialize()/normalize() after queued edits.

The only near-miss was trial-3 choosing WP_HTML_Processor. This did not cause a functional failure, but it shows that the HTML Processor docs can still attract users for a flat construction task because its overview says it safely parses and modifies HTML and its usage appears early. Later passages do say the lighter Tag Processor suffices for flat attribute/class edits and byte-exact preservation, but that guidance could be more visible at the decision point.

doc_gaps.problem: A reader can reach create_fragment() and the general “parse and modify” framing before seeing enough task-selection pressure toward WP_HTML_Tag_Processor for flat template edits.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add an early cross-reference note: for known markup templates, attribute edits, class edits, and byte-preserving output, prefer WP_HTML_Tag_Processor and its “Building markup from a template” recipe; use WP_HTML_Processor when DOM structure, implied elements, breadcrumbs, subtree walks, or normalized serialization matter.

doc_gaps.problem: Trial 3 used inherited Tag Processor mutation methods. The docs mention inherited get_updated_html() in serialization sections, but there is no compact inherited-method summary near the method index.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short “Inherited mutation APIs” section listing inherited set_attribute(), remove_attribute(), set_modifiable_text(), and get_updated_html(), with the contract that queued edits are read via get_updated_html(), not serialize().

doc_gaps.problem: The docs correctly say to check the return value, but examples often omit the check after already guarding on #text. This can leave ambiguity about when ignoring the return is acceptable.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Clarify that a #text-token guard with a known template is sufficient for simple template filling, while generic rewriting code should check the boolean return and choose a fallback when it is false.
